A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PAGE-4D, and their text, equations, tables, and figures are readable. v3 ends after its references despite mentioning an appendix; v4 includes Appendix Sections 6–10. The supplied contents support a reliable comparison, without assuming any unprovided v3 supplement.

before.justification: v3 reports original PAGE-4D depth, camera pose, point reconstruction, rendering, and ablation results in Tables 1–5, with qualitative reconstructions.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and additionally reports numerical architecture diagnostics in Table 7 and learned-mask visualizations in Figure 6.

M1.justification: The main architecture, mask prediction, efficient attention implementation, middle-layer fine-tuning, and losses remain unchanged. Appendix Section 8.1 adds a procedural alternative that removes the dynamic mask during a second training stage instead of retaining it throughout. The existing benchmark results are not assigned to either variant.

E1.justification: v3 leaves the fine-tuning corpus unspecified. v4 Section 9 and Table 8 newly report training coverage spanning CO3D, PointOdyssey, Kubric-MV, DynamicReplica, Spring, Waymo, and RLBench, substantially expanding documented training coverage. This does not establish that the underlying corpus changed between versions. Section 9 also lists Sintel, which Table 8 omits. The principal evaluation benchmarks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 3 removes the Easi3R-DUSt3R and Easi3R-MonST3R comparators from DyCheck point reconstruction. Other benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged. Easi3R remains cited and criticized in the accompanying discussion; the newly cited ManyDepth2 is not added as an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The appendix adds an input-masking control and a comparison of retaining the mask throughout training versus removing it in a second stage. Existing benchmark metrics, depth alignment settings, and the 10-frame, Sim(3)-aligned pose protocol remain unchanged. Newly supplied optimizer settings and details of previously mentioned diagnostics are disclosures, not evidence that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained Table 5 ablations, v4 supplies masking and four-layer perturbation diagnostics in Table 7, parameter-distribution analysis in Table 6, learned-mask inspection in Figure 6, and a mask-schedule comparison. Several analyses were only summarized or referred to an absent appendix in v3. These additions substantially strengthen the documented investigation of the architectural choices.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The retained uncertainty-weighted training losses do not constitute experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v4 substantially expands diagnostic results: Table 7 reports, for example, static depth error of 1.663 after perturbing layer 17 versus 0.085 normally. In Table 1, VGGT's scale-and-shift Sintel Abs Rel/accuracy change from 0.378/0.605 to 0.261/0.639, and DyCheck values change from 0.161/0.778 to 0.155/0.792. PAGE-4D's existing benchmark scores are unchanged. Two Easi3R result rows disappear, while Figures 6–7 add mask outputs and further qualitative reconstructions.

T1.justification: Appendix Section 8.2 adds Equation 8, formally defining the dynamic–dynamic masking matrix through a product of dynamic feature masks. The main geometric reasoning, Equations 1–7, and efficient-attention derivation remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same scientific claims: task-specific treatment of dynamics, targeted fine-tuning, efficient VGGT adaptation, and strong dynamic-scene performance. Revised comparative percentages occur in the results discussion without redefining the central contributions.

C2.justification: The appendix adds interpretations connecting parameter allocation and layer-17 sensitivity to selective fine-tuning, and learned masks to unsupervised separation of motion. Section 6 adds applicability assertions concerning occlusion, fast motion, and illumination changes. The central pose–geometry tension and the stated exclusion of tracking from PAGE-4D remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 adds substantial reproducibility information: dataset sizes and sampling ratios, 518-by-518 resizing, patch size 14, AdamW, learning rate 0.00001, weight decay 0.01, gradient clipping 1.0, and bfloat16 training. It also supplies module parameter counts, diagnostic procedures, video provenance, and a different project-link destination. These are primarily new disclosures; training duration, splits, and the inconsistent inclusion of Sintel remain unresolved.

R1.justification: v4 adds six dataset references supporting the training description and cites ManyDepth2 in the monocular-depth protocol passage. Duplicate Fast3R and spatial-memory references are consolidated rather than representing removed research. The main related-work narrative and positioning against existing 3D/4D approaches remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative is largely retained. Edits correct wording such as 'attention isnice,' ordinal labels, and the monocular-depth table reference; update publication headers and affiliations; and organize the added appendix into Sections 6–10. There is no extensive rewriting or reordering of the existing argument.

P2.justification: v4 adds architecture and training tables, a learned-mask visualization, and a full-page reconstruction montage in Tables 6–8 and Figures 6–7. Table 3 loses two rows and changes result highlighting, while Figure 3 receives localized annotation and caption revisions. The original main figures and overall main-text layout are largely retained.

improvement.justification: v4 improves transparency by supplying previously unavailable masking and layer diagnostics, learned-mask examples, and useful training details. The gain is limited by the unexplained removal of Easi3R results while retaining criticism of that method, and by the disagreement between Section 9 and Table 8 about Sintel training data with no split clarification. The added support provides a modest net benefit, while PAGE-4D's existing benchmark scores and central claims remain unchanged.
